release.body:
## [0.9.1](https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora/compare/0.9.0...0.9.1) - 2026-11-02


**🐛 Bug Fixes**

* Fix a panic on every accepted and outgoing connection with tokio 1.54 and later, which rejects zero-capacity buffered readers (#1059).
* Fix the docs.rs build of the `pingora` crate, which failed for 0.9.0 (#1018).
* Fix a panic in `pingora-limits` `Estimator::incr` when a counter overflows in builds with overflow checks enabled (#1041).

**🔒 Security**

* Require zstd 0.14.3, and through it zstd-safe 8.2.0 and zstd-sys 2.1.2, so dependency resolution cannot select zstd crates affected by RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0395 through RUSTSEC-2026-0406, or RUSTSEC-2026-0410.

**⚙️ Miscellaneous Tasks**

* Ignore RustSec advisories for rustls 0.21, webpki-roots 0.26, rustls-webpki 0.101 and crypto-bigint 0.5.5, which reach the lockfile only through optional transitive dependencies and have no compatible fixed release.
* Update HTTP/2 rejection tests for h2 releases that reject conflicting Content-Length headers in the codec.

pull_request.title: feat(http1): expose configurable request-header parser admission limits (#993)
pull_request.body:
### Description

This PR addresses #993 by exposing configurable request-header admission limits (`max_header_size` and `max_headers`) on `HttpServerOptions`, propagating them through `ServerSession` to the underlying HTTP/1 `HttpSession`.

### Motivation

In HTTP/1.x downstream servers, Pingora previously enforced hardcoded limits:
- `MAX_HEADER_SIZE`: 1,048,575 bytes (~1 MiB)
- `MAX_HEADERS`: 256 headers

For reverse proxies and security-sensitive gateways, rejecting oversized headers only in downstream application filters (e.g. `request_filter`) is often too late: the server has already buffered up to 1 MiB of untrusted header bytes into memory per connection. Enforcing configurable admission bounds directly in `HttpSession::read_request()` prevents memory exhaustion and slowloris-style buffer bloat before request processing begins. Conversely, proxies operating in trusted environments can adjust limits appropriately.

### Key Changes

1. **`HttpServerOptions`**:
   - Added `pub max_header_size: Option<usize>` (bytes limit).
   - Added `pub max_headers: Option<usize>` (header count limit).
   - Added `validate(&self) -> Result<()>` checking that neither limit is set to `Some(0)`.

2. **Session Layer Accessors**:
   - Added `set_max_header_size`, `max_header_size`, `set_max_headers`, and `max_headers` on `ServerSession` and `HttpSession`.

3. **Zero-Allocation Parser Admission (`HttpSession::read_request`)**:
   - **Initial allocation:** Bounds initial buffer capacity to `INIT_HEADER_BUF_SIZE.min(max_header_size)`.
   - **Slow bloat guard:** Replaced hardcoded `MAX_HEADER_SIZE` guard with `already_read > max_header_size`.
   - **Count limit:** Slices the stack-allocated header array `&mut headers[..max_headers]` when constructing `httparse::Request`. This enforces the count limit on the stack with zero heap allocations, returning `InvalidHTTPHeader` via httparse's `TooManyHeaders`.
   - **Single packet guard:** Checks `if s > max_header_size` in `HeaderParseState::Complete(s)` to prevent large single-chunk reads or pipelined prefixes from exceeding limits.

4. **Keep-Alive Preservation**:
   - Propagates `server_options.max_header_size` and `server_options.max_headers` across reused connections in `HttpServerApp::process_new`.

5. **Backward Compatibility**:
   - Both settings default to `None`. When unset, existing defaults (`MAX_HEADER_SIZE = 1,048,575` bytes and `MAX_HEADERS = 256`) remain strictly intact.

### Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
- `test_max_header_size_within_limit`: Valid request within custom size limit parses successfully.
- `test_max_header_size_exceeded_multi_chunk`: Request exceeding limit across multiple chunks is rejected with `InvalidHTTPHeader`.
- `test_max_header_size_exceeded_single_chunk`: Complete request exceeding limit in a single read is rejected.
- `test_max_header_size_pipelined_prefix`: Pipelined prefix exceeding limit is rejected.
- `test_max_headers_within_limit`: Header count within custom limit succeeds.
- `test_max_headers_exceeded`: Exceeding header count limit rejects with `InvalidHTTPHeader`.
- `test_default_limits_preserved`: Default configuration preserves existing behavior.
- `test_http_server_options_validation`: Validates non-zero bounds on options.

Closes #993

pull_request.title: refactor(core): replace the unmaintained serde_yaml with serde-saphyr (RUSTSEC-2024-0449)
pull_request.body:
Refs #779 (replace the deprecated `serde_yaml`; the maintainers' answer there was that they would). Fixes #1058 (RUSTSEC-2024-0449).

## Why

`serde_yaml` is archived, and it pulls in `unsafe-libyaml`, which the advisory RUSTSEC-2024-0449 reports as unmaintained. It reaches every downstream project through `pingora-core`, so each of them has to ignore the advisory (#1058). `serde-saphyr` is safe Rust, maintained, and the replacement the advisory suggests.

## What

- `pingora-core`: `ServerConf::from_yaml` and `ServerConf::to_yaml` use `serde_saphyr::from_str` / `to_string`. The API of `pingora-core` does not change.
- `pingora-proxy`: the `modify_response` example (and the dev-dependency) uses `serde_saphyr::to_string`.
- The one test that inspected a `serde_yaml::Value` (`test_working_directory_deserializes_from_yaml_string`) now checks the written yaml and that it reads back as the same configuration.
- A second commit changes the CI toolchain matrix (see below).

`serde_yaml` and `unsafe-libyaml` are gone from the dependency tree of `pingora-core` and `pingora-proxy` (`cargo tree -i unsafe-libyaml` finds nothing).

## The MSRV (please read)

`serde-saphyr` uses let chains and declares `rust-version = "1.89"` (its releases from 1.2.0 on; 1.1.0 declares nothing but already fails on 1.85 with `error[E0658]: let expressions in this position are unstable`). The job that checks the oldest toolchain, 1.85.0, therefore cannot build `pingora-core` with it. This was the question raised in #779 ("it requires rust 1.89").

I kept that change in its own commit, so it is easy to drop or rework: the oldest toolchain in `.github/workflows/build.yml` becomes `1.89.0` (same exclusions as before), and `pingora-cache`, which declares a `rust-version` and depends on `pingora-core`, declares `1.89`. I did not touch `clippy.toml` (`msrv = "1.85"`), because changing it can enable new lints, which is a separate decision. If you prefer to keep 1.85, the alternative is a maintained fork of the same libyaml port (for example `serde_norway`), which keeps the C-translated parser and may build on 1.85; I did not try it. Tell me which way you prefer and I will rework the PR.

## Checked

- `cargo test -p pingora-core --lib server::configuration`: 14 passed, on stable (1.99.1, Linux).
- `cargo check -p pingora-core -p pingora-proxy -p pingora-cache -p pingora-load-balancing --all-targets` and `cargo check -p pingora-proxy --example modify_response` on 1.89.0 and on stable.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- Not run here: `cargo check --workspace` (the BoringSSL crates need libclang, which my machine lacks), the TLS-backend tests, the 1.89.0 test leg of CI.

# unsafe-libyaml is unmaintained

The [repository](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) was archived by
its owner on 2024-03-25 and is read-only. The last release is 0.2.11
(March 2024).

`unsafe-libyaml` is a machine translation of libyaml's C code into unsafe
Rust (c2rust). Bugs found in it will not be fixed upstream. It is used by
`serde_yaml` (itself deprecated) and by forks such as `serde_yaml_ng`.

## Alternatives

Consider a YAML parser written in safe Rust, for example:

- [saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/saphyr) ([serde-saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/serde-saphyr) for serde users)
- [noyalib](https://crates.io/crates/noyalib)
